import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_4.csv"
source5_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_5.csv"
source6_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_6.csv"
source7_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_7.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Influenced']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Spotify']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Score']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source5_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Times on Cover of RS']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source6_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source7_path, index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Certified Units (Millions)']

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source6_9_0", "Source6_9_6"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_1 = pd.merge(df0, df6, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 2) JOIN : [["Source6_9_1", "Source6_9_2"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_2 = pd.merge(df1, df2, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 3) JOIN : [["Source6_9_3", "Source6_9_4"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_3 = pd.merge(df3, df4, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 4) JOIN : [["Source6_9_5", "Source6_9_7"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_4 = pd.merge(df5, df7, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 5) JOIN : [["Source6_9_6", "Source6_9_0"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
# This is the same join as #1 but reversed order, so join_1 and join_5 are the same.
# To follow the operation strictly, we do it again:
join_5 = pd.merge(df6, df0, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 6) JOIN : [["Source6_9_6", "Source6_9_7"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_6 = pd.merge(df6, df7, on="Artist", how="inner")

# Now we have these intermediate joins:
# join_1: df0 + df6
# join_2: df1 + df2
# join_3: df3 + df4
# join_4: df5 + df7
# join_5: df6 + df0 (same as join_1 but reversed)
# join_6: df6 + df7

# To produce the final target table Target6_9, we need to combine all source tables.
# The target schema columns are:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': integer,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float,
#  'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer,
#  'Highest Position': integer,
#  'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float,
#  'Spotify': integer]

# We have partial data in each join:
# join_1 and join_5 contain: Artist, Influenced, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
# join_2 contains: Artist, Spotify, Albums in RS500
# join_3 contains: Artist, Top 100 Singles, Highest Position, Score
# join_4 contains: Artist, Times on Cover of RS, Certified Units (Millions)
# join_6 contains: Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Certified Units (Millions)

# We must join all these results on Artist to get all columns.

# Start by joining join_1 and join_2 on Artist
df_temp1 = pd.merge(join_1, join_2, on="Artist", how="outer")

# Join df_temp1 with join_3 on Artist
df_temp2 = pd.merge(df_temp1, join_3, on="Artist", how="outer")

# Join df_temp2 with join_4 on Artist
df_temp3 = pd.merge(df_temp2, join_4, on="Artist", how="outer")

# join_5 is same as join_1 but reversed, no new info, skip to avoid duplication

# join_6 overlaps with join_1 and join_4, but join_4 already has Certified Units (Millions)
# join_6 has Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Certified Units (Millions)
# join_4 has Times on Cover of RS, Certified Units (Millions)
# join_1 has Influenced, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
# join_6 can add no new columns that are not already in df_temp3, so skip join_6 to avoid duplication

# After these merges, df_temp3 should have all columns from all sources.

# Now, ensure all columns from target schema exist in df_temp3, fill missing columns with appropriate types and default values

target_columns = [
    'Artist',
    'Year Inducted',
    'Years Waited',
    '# of Years Nominated',
    'Influenced',
    'Certified Units (Millions)',
    'Albums in RS500',
    'Top 100 Singles',
    'Highest Position',
    'Times on Cover of RS',
    'Score',
    'Spotify'
]

# Add missing columns if any, with NaNs
for col in target_columns:
    if col not in df_temp3.columns:
        df_temp3[col] = pd.NA

# Reorder columns to target schema order
df_final = df_temp3[target_columns]

# Data type corrections and filling missing values:
# From target examples, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Influenced, Albums in RS500,
# Top 100 Singles, Highest Position, Times on Cover of RS, Spotify are integers
# Certified Units (Millions), Score are floats
# Artist is string

# Convert Artist to string and strip whitespace if any
df_final['Artist'] = df_final['Artist'].astype(str).str.strip()

# For integer columns, convert to Int64 (nullable integer) to allow NaNs
int_cols = [
    'Year Inducted',
    'Years Waited',
    '# of Years Nominated',
    'Influenced',
    'Albums in RS500',
    'Top 100 Singles',
    'Highest Position',
    'Times on Cover of RS',
    'Spotify'
]
for col in int_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# For float columns
float_cols = ['Certified Units (Millions)', 'Score']
for col in float_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

# Optional: If any NaNs in numeric columns, fill with 0 or appropriate default
# Based on target examples, 0 is a reasonable default for missing numeric values
df_final[int_cols] = df_final[int_cols].fillna(0)
df_final[float_cols] = df_final[float_cols].fillna(0.0)

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/target_multisource.csv"
df_final.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_7.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all tables on 'Artist' using source6 as the central table (dimension table)
df = source6.merge(source0, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source7, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source2, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source3, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source5, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source4, on="Artist", how="left") \
            .merge(source1, on="Artist", how="left")

# Fill NaN with 0 for numeric columns to allow aggregation
numeric_cols = ['Influenced', 'Certified Units (Millions)', 'Albums in RS500', 'Top 100 Singles', 
                'Highest Position', 'Times on Cover of RS', 'Score', 'Spotify']
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in df.columns:
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0)

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns that appear to be unique identifiers in target examples
group_by_cols = ["Artist", "Year Inducted", "Years Waited", "# of Years Nominated"]

# Aggregate by sum for all other columns (excluding group by columns)
agg_dict = {
    "Influenced": "sum",
    "Certified Units (Millions)": "sum",
    "Albums in RS500": "sum",
    "Top 100 Singles": "sum",
    "Highest Position": "sum",
    "Times on Cover of RS": "sum",
    "Score": "sum",
    "Spotify": "sum"
}

df_final = df.groupby(group_by_cols, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Ensure columns are in the exact order as target schema
target_columns = ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Influenced', 
                  'Certified Units (Millions)', 'Albums in RS500', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position', 
                  'Times on Cover of RS', 'Score', 'Spotify']

df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Write to the target file
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
